newsitem.title: USA: LodgeNet Q4 loss widens but EBITDA is up.
newsitem.headline: LodgeNet Q4 loss widens but EBITDA is up.

text.p: LodgeNet Entertainment Corp, a specialized communications company providing video on demand, said its fourth-quarter loss, including a charge for early redemption of notes, widened over the same year-ago period, although earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization rose significantly.
It said EBITDA rose in the quarter to $6.2 million from $4.4 million largely as a result of increasing revenues from Guest Pay services.

By year-end 1996, LodgeNet said its Guest Pay room base exceeded 400,000, growing by 49 percent during the year. Average monthly revenue per Guest Pay room, including movie and video game-information service revenue, increased 8.9 percent to $20.70 in 1996's fourth quarter from $19.01 in the same 1995 period.

Chief operating officer Scott Petersen said, "Because of the strong cash flow we are generating in our core lodging business and our successful $150 million senior note offering in December, we are in an excellent position to execute our plans for continued aggressive growth."
LodgeNet said total operating expenses for 1996's fourth quarter increased to $17.6 million from $10.7 million.

For the quarter, LodgeNet posted a loss of $0.76 per share, including a $0.29 per share loss from early redemption of notes, compared to a year-earlier loss of $0.38 per share. Quarterly sales advanced to $27.0 million from $17.8 million.

President Tim Flynn said the company in 1996 laid the groundwork for a new revenue source through its ResNet Communications subsidiary, created to apply LodgeNet's b-LAN systems platform to the multifamily residential market.
"ResNet enters 1997 with a revised growth strategy that does not rely exclusively on the acquisition of new contracts," he said.
